Hi Samira — great to meet you and Rajiv on the call. Recap + next steps below.

Quick recap of what we heard:
- Primary workload: user-facing triage and short-answer extraction from support transcripts.
- Key constraints: low-latency (sub-300ms target for single-turn UI), and PHI-sensitive fields in some queries (need redaction audit).

Recommended starter models (tradeoffs):
- redwood-optim-7b-quant (recommended for balanced latency/cost) — ~150–220ms p99 on 8xA100 equivalent; best for conversational throughput.
- open-instruct-13b-8bit (higher quality for extraction tasks but higher cost/latency).
- redwood-3.2b-lowlat (lowest cost, good for short completion prompts; expect slightly lower extractive accuracy).

I attached our one-page benchmark summary (redwood-eval-benchmarks-20270401.pdf) — it shows token-cost, typical latency ranges, and suggested prompt shapes for extraction vs. generative replies. Link to the same doc: https://drive.google.com/redwood/drive/eval/benchmarks-20270401

For prompt/edge-case collection we ask for:
1) A CSV with one user query per row; include a short context field where relevant (conversation snippet).
2) Flag any rows that contain PHI/PII so Ben and Laura can prioritize redaction guidance.
3) Examples of failure cases you care about (e.g., hallucinated medication names, mis-extracted dates, long-thread context >5 turns).

Privacy & upload: we prefer a secure, access-restricted Drive folder or SFTP — I can share a link with edit access for just your team.

Next steps / timeline:
- Please drop a 400–800 query sample (CSV) and a short list of 10 high-priority edge cases.
- Ben will share a redaction checklist and we’ll run an initial benchmark on the 3 model configurations (target turn-around: 5 business days after we receive the sample).

If you want, I can also scope a small A/B eval (two model configs) and return token-level cost projections for a 30k-token/day baseline.

Thanks — I’ll await the sample.

Chloe Martin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-eval-benchmarks-20270401.pdf (1 page PDF)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: VectorHealth discovery — eval materials & scenario bank request

Looping in a few quick redaction pointers before you upload the sample:

- Please remove or flag direct identifiers (SSN, full MRN) — we can accept pseudonymized IDs (e.g., user_XX).
- Leave high-level clinical terms ("chest pain", "blood glucose") — those are okay for model fit.
- If possible, replace free-text spans that include phone numbers / credit-card-like numbers with <REDACTED_PHONE> / <REDACTED_CC>.
- Regex we commonly use for initial scanning: \b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b (SSN-like), \b\d{10,16}\b (long numeric sequences).

I attached a short internal guide (vh-sensitive-field-redaction-guide.pdf) that you can share with your data owner — it has an example redaction script and a checklist for manual review. If you need, we can run a privacy-scan pass (small fee) before doing the benchmark.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: vh-sensitive-field-redaction-guide.pdf (3 pages PDF)
